svg.text: TRANSIT RESEARCH BRIEFING
Daily Transit Intelligence
June 27, 2026 — 15 papers analyzed
KEY FINDINGS
A counterfactual-without-control-group method finds NYC congestion pricing lifted bus and subway
ridership well beyond the priced zone, while overall travel demand fell only modestly and unevenly
across neighborhoods -- the first rigorous post-implementation read of the policy.
A new dynamic program computes provable worst-case (not average-case) bus headway bounds, applied
to a real Nashville route -- the first tool to bound the longest possible rider wait under any
holding policy, not just the typical one.
A decade-old SUMO mesoscopic traffic model is shown to violate core flow theory and systematically
underestimate congestion, calling into question prior congestion-dependent transit research that
relied on it.
PAPER OF THE DAY
Optimizing Accessibility and Maximum Travel Times in Transit Networks: The Hub Covering Lo
Carmen-Ana Domínguez-Bravo, Elena Fernández, Armin Lüer-Villagra
A new mixed-integer optimization model places transit access points and hub corridors to jointly cap
first/last-mile travel time and total trip time across a network.
It's the freshest submission in today's batch (June 25) and reframes a classic OR problem in a way
that matters operationally: instead of optimizing coverage or speed alone, it makes the first/last-
mile access-time ceiling an explicit, tunable design parameter alongside trunk-network speed, giving

ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS
Agencies citing SUMO-mesoscopic-derived congestion forecasts for BRT or signal-priority corridor
decisions should treat congestion-magnitude estimates as likely understated until the corrected
Before expanding fare-free programs, use scenario simulation (like the NYC fare framework) to
separate the equity case from the ridership case — they are not the same argument and shouldn't be
Agencies designing or revising bus holding policies should evaluate them against worst-case headway
bounds, not just average headway, since average-case-optimized policies can still produce bad worst-
Low-density and rural transit agencies evaluating microtransit/DRT vendors should ask whether
dispatch is centralized or decentralized — the slime-mold results suggest decentralized bidding
